messages:
jia: Quick sync — proposing we parcellate the runtime-control surface into smaller "parcels" so teams can iterate on hotpath optimizations independently. RFC linked: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2023-parcellation :point_right: TL;DR: split responsibilities (routing/cache/exec) behind a thin facade, keep a single tenancy model.
kevin: curious — what's the primary win? faster deploys or lower cognitive load?
marta: main win is lower blast radius for changes to KV/cache warming logic. currently a small tweak in runtime touches routing and session code.
sam: also means smaller deploy units for perf experiments. but cost: more RPC hops and duplicated logic if we don't centralize some helpers.
jia: correct — tradeoff is RPC overhead vs. service autonomy. my rough acceptance criteria: no >5ms median increase on P50 for token path, canary migration path, and clear ownership for cached prefixes.
eli: +1 on ownership. also we should avoid duplicating model-profile state — reuse the model-profile-registry read-only view.
marta: cache ownership is tricky. if parcel A owns KV cache for prefixes, how do we handle cross-parcel requests? ideas: a) single cache service (shared), b) per-parcel caches with async replication, c) request routing to parcel owning prefix. each has perf/consistency tradeoffs.
kevin: option (c) keeps fast reads but complicates routing table. option (a) centralizes: lower duplication but single hop. I'm leaning (a) for now with future split if perf demands.
sam: operationally we should plan for a facade that multiplexes to either central cache or per-parcel caches so we can A/B. facade buys rollback safety. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: FYI deploy-bot started a canary branch job: canary/parcellation-v1 on infra-qa cluster. Logs: https://ci.internal/build/4387
jia: Proposal for incremental cutover (sketch):
  1) Define minimal stable RPC contract (gRPC) for parcel boundary (routing + cache lookup + exec intent).
  2) Implement facade shim in runtime that delegates to current monolith OR new parcel implementation based on header flag.
  3) Wire parcel to use read-only model-profile-registry (no writes).
  4) Canary at 5% traffic for 48h, collect p50/p95, CPU/GPU tails, and cache hit-rate.
  5) If perf/regressions OK, increase to 25% then 100% with automated rollback on error budget breach.
kevin: what's our signal for "perf/regressions OK" specifically? SLOs or relative delta?
jia: both. SLOs must hold (latency and error rate). plus cost delta must be within X% (TBD). for initial canary, compare 24h p95 delta and cache hit-rate.
marta: need test harness to simulate warm KV prefixes; otherwise canary will be cold and give false negatives. I can add a workload generator spike in the QA run.
eli: also plan telemetry: token-level tracing across facade -> parcel -> cache to root-cause added latency. add a lightweight trace-id header.
sam: proto sketch (very rough):
```
service ParcelService {
  rpc FetchTokenContext(FetchReq) returns (FetchReply);
}
message FetchReq {
  string session_id = 1;
  string tenant_id = 2;
  bool prefer_central_cache = 3;
}
message FetchReply {
  bytes kv_payload = 1;
  bool cache_hit = 2;
  int64 backend_latency_ms = 3;
}
```
kevin: looks fine as a starting point. need auth headers and budget hints later.
ops-bot: note: created ticket INF-1182 for canary observability dashboards (p50/p95/cpu/gpu/hotpath-ms).
jia: next steps: assign owners for parcel API, facade shim, and telemetry. propose owners: API: kevin, facade: sam, telemetry + harness: marta. confirm?
kevin: I can take API.
sam: I'll own the facade.
marta: will do telemetry and harness.
eli: I'll help with model-profile integration and runbook entries.
jia: great. I'll update RFC with the incremental plan and add the proto sketch + runbook links. we should schedule a short sync next week after first QA canary completes. :calendar:
kevin: one more note — consider per-tenant sticky routing so session affinity doesn't cross parcels; failure mode emergency plan needed.
marta: added to INF-1182 as a checklist item.
eli: cool. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: canary job completed (status: success). artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/4387
jia: thanks everyone. I'll post RFC update and an outline of the rollback playbook later today.
kevin: thanks — excited to see this reduce churn.
eli: happy to pair on the final integration tests.
